overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law on October 21 by holding an improper Purpose 2 executive session to discuss a law firm contract and by posting a notice too vague to reveal that topic; no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee improperly met in executive session on October 21 to discuss retaining a law firm to investigate a football game incident.
allegations.key_passage: A discussion of vendor or service contracts, such as retaining a law firm, is not appropriate for executive session under Purpose 2 and as such the Committee’s discussion should have taken place during an open session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the October 21 meeting notice did not sufficiently inform the public that the law firm retention would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: the notice for the October 21 meeting did not include any topic, whether for open session or executive session, that would have reasonably advised the public that the Committee anticipated discussing retaining a law firm to conduct an investigation

allegations.summary: Complainant urged a finding that the committee intentionally violated the Open Meeting Law, citing an earlier determination against it.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find that the Committee intentionally violated the Law.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the notice failed to name the nonunion personnel to be discussed in executive session under Purpose 2.
allegations.key_passage: public bodies should identify, both in their notice and in the open session announcement made before entering executive session, the name of the specific nonunion personnel that is the subject of discussion under Purpose 2

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: executive session minutes were very brief and may not summarize the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Where this issue was not raised in a complaint and not fully investigated, we make no finding as to whether the minutes of the October 21 executive session were sufficiently detailed

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Release to the public the executive session minutes and any documents used during the executive session, such as the contract, if not already done.
Each Committee member must review the Attorney General's executive session training video, with certification to the office within 30 days.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
